items.summary_original: President Donald Trump told Fox News' "Saturday in America" that outgoing Texas Sen. John Cornyn is doing a "tremendous disservice" by blocking his pick to fill a judicial seat in Dallas. The president said, "We're going to have a radical left lunatic get in there and we don't want that." Trump's comments come after Cornyn told The Associated Press he has no intention of returning the "blue slip" for T. Elliot Gaiser, a Department of Justice senior lawyer who was nominated by the president to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas. The blue slip tradition allows for home state senators to weigh in on judicial nominees, giving them a say on who does and doesn’t move forward. Returning a blue slip is the equivalent of giving a thumbs up to the nominees moving forward, while keeping the slip effectively blocks the process. "Everybody tells me he's outstanding and he's being held up by John Cornyn because John Cornyn's feelings were hurt," said Trump, who endorsed Cornyn's challenger Ken Paxton in the Texas Republican Senate primary. The FBI is investigating the hack to determine the unauthorized entry point, but for now, it is unclear what information was compromised, sources said. The NCIC database is a critical information-sharing tool for federal, state and local authorities, helping them track fugitives, monitor registered sex offenders, check whether someone has failed a gun background check, among many other things. In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. CNN first reported the hack. In September, a group called ShinyHunters hacked into the FBI's job portal website intending to steal sensitive employment records. Rising from the barren Nevada desert, the Crescent Dunes Solar Energy Project looks like a futuristic fortress in a vast, dusty wasteland, with more than 10,000 mirrors surrounding a giant central tower. The plant was designed to generate solar electricity even after sunset, using an emerging technology that promised to revolutionize green energy in America . items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting. He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe. "We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said. The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks . On Tuesday, Iran also claimed responsibility for another strike on a U.S. military base in Bahrain, its third attack there in five days. The Army plans to build 10 bunkers in Israel, five in Saudi Arabia and two in Lebanon, replacing makeshift shelters made from shipping containers. "Due to elevated regional force protection conditions, there is an urgent, high-priority requirement to replace nonstandard personnel protection shelters (e.g., converted shipping containers) and provide standardized, precast, reinforced concrete Indirect Fire bunkers," the Army said in the notice. items.summary_original: Hundreds of Iranians took to the streets chanting "Death to the dictator!" and other anti-government messages in the wake of a deadly bus crash over the weekend that killed 13 employees of an oil refinery company, reports said. The rare display of anti-government anger unfolded Tuesday in Abdanan, a city in western Iran near the country's border with Iraq. Demonstrators called for the resignation of company officials blamed for the accident. "Those who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order and inflame people’s emotions will be dealt with decisively," local prosecutor Amrollah Meysaei was quoted by Iran's Mizan news agency as saying, according to Radio Free Europe. The outlet, citing Iran's Fars news agency, also reported that an estimated 1,000 people took part in the protests, making them the largest demonstrations since mass unrest swept across Iran at the beginning of this year. Some of the protesters reportedly tried to damage public property.
